name: ai-ready
desc: Free, open-source AI readiness check for Windows — GPU, VRAM and runtime verdicts plus model suggestions. 100 MB portable, offline, MIT.
features: ✅ **Hardware verdicts** — GPU, VRAM, RAM and CPU flags checked against the real needs of local models
✅ **Tool-class matrix** — see whether a 7B chat model, image generation or Whisper will run well, barely or not
✅ **Runtime support check** — CUDA, Vulkan and DirectML availability reported before you download gigabytes
✅ **Bottleneck callout** — one plain sentence names the part holding the machine back, usually VRAM
✅ **Model size suggestions** — concrete quant and context ceilings for this exact machine
✅ **Shareable report** — a text summary for forum posts and support threads with serials redacted
✅ **100 MB self-contained exe** — runtime bundled, portable, fully offline, MIT with SHA-256 releases
compare: | Feature | **ai-ready** | dxdiag | GPU-Z | Forum checklist posts |
| Local AI capability verdict | **Yes** | No | No | Manual
| Runtime matrix CUDA Vulkan DirectML | **Yes** | No | Partial | No
| Model size suggestions | **Yes** | No | No | Rough
| Portable, no install | **Yes, 100 MB** | Built-in | Installer | N/A
faqQ: can my PC run local LLMs? which model size fits my GPU?
faqA: Forum answers range from wrong to insulting, and guesswork wastes gigabytes of downloads. ai-ready checks the actual hardware and runtimes, then gives concrete quant and context ceilings plus a bottleneck sentence. It is a 100 MB portable exe, MIT, offline, with a redacted report you can paste anywhere.
s1: Dark readiness report (#121418, emerald #059669): green check rows for GPU, RAM and runtime probes, verdict card reading 13B models run well, 70B not.
s2: Tool matrix: rows for chat, image generation, speech and OCR with status badges from smooth to not viable, legend panel on the right.
s3: Suggestions panel: quant ceiling Q5_K_M noted, context advice at 16k, bottleneck sentence about 8 GB VRAM, export report button highlighted.
